question: How do the portfolio's valuations compare with public peers?
html:
Portfolio valuations versus public peers

The context cannot answer this directly. It holds no current valuation or entry multiple for any BSP portfolio company, apart from an est. ~12-15x entry for Frontline. It also holds no EV/EBITDA trading multiples for the 31 public peers. What it does support is a comparison of operating economics against public peers and of deal-multiple ranges from private transactions.

What the evidence shows

CompanyPublic peer economicsPrivate multiple evidenceQuality premium (est.)
Punctual ProsResidential median: 13.6% growth, 14.4% operating margin. Installers IBP and BLD flat (Public comparables)PKF 5-6x vs 10x+. Champions ~18.5x, Sila ~17x (press estimates)1.0-2.5 turns
CETCommercial electrical median: 6.4% operating margin, ~11.2% EBITDA. FIX 14.4%, IESC 11.4% (Public comparables)PKF grid; Capstone 6.8x vs 9.8x0.5-1.5 turns
FrontlineOnshore services (CBIZ $290k per employee) earn 3-9% operating margins (Public comparables)Aventis MSP 5.2x-11.2x; entry ~12-15x (est.)0.5-1.5 turns
Thomas ScientificAvantor ~80% digital transactionsNo disclosed multiple premium0.5-1.0 turns
BPIAgencies median +0.3% growth; WPP -8.1%PPHC ~8.4x floor vs 10-13x est. sponsor exit0.5-2.0 turns

Premium ranges are from the ServiceOS evidence. Fair Harbor's range is cut off in the source.

How to read it

  • Frontline may already be priced near the top. Its est. ~12-15x entry sits above the Aventis 11.2x top of curve. Further multiple gain will need churn and recurring-revenue proof.
  • Trades value comes from mix. Public margins are thin, so CET and Punctual Pros gain through service, membership and mission-critical work, not price (Public comparables).
  • Scale drives the headline prints. Roll-up prints of 17-20x come from scale and density. Tech enablement can claim only about 0.5-2.5 turns (ServiceOS evidence).
  • Thomas Scientific is an EBITDA story. Capital structure dominates its exit. Leverage gains matter more than multiple gains.
  • Caveats apply. Public EBITDA here is operating income plus D&A, not Adjusted EBITDA. The Champions and Sila multiples are unconfirmed press estimates.

Data that would close the gap

  • Public peer EV/EBITDA and EV/revenue multiples, pulled on one date.
  • BSP entry multiples and latest marks for each portfolio company.
  • Each portfolio company's growth, margin and revenue per employee, on the same unadjusted basis as the peers.

Next actions

  1. Add trading multiples to the Public comparables set, refreshed on one date. Map them to each portfolio company.
  2. Pull entry and current-mark multiples from fund records, starting with the Frontline entry estimate.
  3. Restate each portfolio company's EBITDA on an operating income plus D&A basis so it compares cleanly with peers.
  4. Complete the Fair Harbor premium range and peer set before the next portfolio review.

# Portfolio valuations versus public peers

The context cannot answer this directly. It holds no current valuation or entry multiple for any BSP portfolio company, apart from an est. ~12-15x entry for Frontline. It also holds no EV/EBITDA trading multiples for the 31 public peers. What it does support is a comparison of operating economics against public peers and of deal-multiple ranges from private transactions.

## What the evidence shows

| Company | Public peer economics | Private multiple evidence | Quality premium (est.) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Punctual Pros | Residential median: 13.6% growth, 14.4% operating margin. Installers IBP and BLD flat (Public comparables) | PKF 5-6x vs 10x+. Champions ~18.5x, Sila ~17x (press estimates) | 1.0-2.5 turns |
| CET | Commercial electrical median: 6.4% operating margin, ~11.2% EBITDA. FIX 14.4%, IESC 11.4% (Public comparables) | PKF grid; Capstone 6.8x vs 9.8x | 0.5-1.5 turns |
| Frontline | Onshore services (CBIZ $290k per employee) earn 3-9% operating margins (Public comparables) | Aventis MSP 5.2x-11.2x; entry ~12-15x (est.) | 0.5-1.5 turns |
| Thomas Scientific | Avantor ~80% digital transactions | No disclosed multiple premium | 0.5-1.0 turns |
| BPI | Agencies median +0.3% growth; WPP -8.1% | PPHC ~8.4x floor vs 10-13x est. sponsor exit | 0.5-2.0 turns |

Premium ranges are from the ServiceOS evidence. Fair Harbor's range is cut off in the source.

## How to read it

- **Frontline may already be priced near the top.** Its est. ~12-15x entry sits above the Aventis 11.2x top of curve. Further multiple gain will need churn and recurring-revenue proof.
- **Trades value comes from mix.** Public margins are thin, so CET and Punctual Pros gain through service, membership and mission-critical work, not price (Public comparables).
- **Scale drives the headline prints.** Roll-up prints of 17-20x come from scale and density. Tech enablement can claim only about 0.5-2.5 turns (ServiceOS evidence).
- **Thomas Scientific is an EBITDA story.** Capital structure dominates its exit. Leverage gains matter more than multiple gains.
- **Caveats apply.** Public EBITDA here is operating income plus D&A, not Adjusted EBITDA. The Champions and Sila multiples are unconfirmed press estimates.

## Data that would close the gap

- Public peer EV/EBITDA and EV/revenue multiples, pulled on one date.
- BSP entry multiples and latest marks for each portfolio company.
- Each portfolio company's growth, margin and revenue per employee, on the same unadjusted basis as the peers.

## Next actions

1. Add trading multiples to the Public comparables set, refreshed on one date. Map them to each portfolio company.
2. Pull entry and current-mark multiples from fund records, starting with the Frontline entry estimate.
3. Restate each portfolio company's EBITDA on an operating income plus D&A basis so it compares cleanly with peers.
4. Complete the Fair Harbor premium range and peer set before the next portfolio review.
